analysis.investment_thesis: Unified Data fails both pillars of the Magic Formula: earnings yield of ~4.7% (1/21.1 P/E) is below my 6% floor, and ROE of 0.36% signals near-zero return on capital. Neither cheap nor good — a clear pass.
key_strengths: Operates in asset-light IT services (structurally capable of high ROIC)
Small market cap (INR 619 Cr) allows room for growth if execution improves
key_risks: ROE of 0.36% implies capital is essentially being destroyed vs cost of equity
P/E 21.1 on near-zero profitability is extremely expensive on an earnings-yield basis
Tiny FII (0.57%) and DII (5.89%) float — low institutional validation and liquidity
red_flags: ROE <1% — ROIC almost certainly fails the >20% Magic Formula threshold
Earnings yield ~4.7% is below the 6% overvalued cutoff
Possible recent IPO/cash-drag inflating equity base and depressing returns
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The Magic Formula ranks companies on the intersection of cheapness (EBIT/EV) and quality (EBIT/Capital). Unified Data flunks both. A trailing P/E of 21.1 translates to an earnings yield of roughly 4.7% — well below the 6% minimum I consider, let alone the 12%+ I want for a buy. Simultaneously, an ROE of just 0.36% strongly suggests ROIC is nowhere near the 20%+ I demand; the company is earning essentially nothing on shareholders' capital. This is the worst quadrant: expensive and low-quality.

The only plausible rehabilitation would be if the low ROE reflects fresh IPO proceeds sitting in cash (the BSE listing is recent) and operating ROIC ex-cash is materially higher — but that's speculation, not a systematic buy signal. Until EBIT grows into the capital base and the earnings yield expands above 10%, this does not screen for the Magic Formula basket. Avoid.
